in Goa|date=25 June 2016|work=Business Standard|access-date=28 April 2017|agency=Press Trust of India}} ==History== ===Sterlite Industries=== '''Vedanta''' (then called '''Sterlite industries''') began in the 1980s, as the founder D. P. Agarwal founded '''Sterlite Industries (India) Limited''' in [[Mumbai]] and begun to buy [[Mining in India|mining concessions]] in different states of India. He was soon joined by his two sons, Navin Agarwal and Anil Agarwal, both of whom currently run the company. In 1992, they established Volcan investments in [[Nassau, Bahamas|Nassau]] ([[Bahamas]]) as the main holding company for their mines.{{cite news |last1=thakurta |first1=Prananjoy Guha |title=Vedanta's Questionable Resources |url=https://www.minesandcommunities.org/article.php?a=9685 |access-date=17 October 2018 |publisher=Current Weekly |date=2 November 2009}} D. P. Agarwal had a small aluminium conductor business in [[Patna]]. His son [[Anil Agarwal (industrialist)|Anil Agarwal]] had come to Mumbai to expand their business.{{cite news |last1=Kumar |first1=Rohit |title=NCLT approves Vedanta's resolution plan for Electrosteel (Lead) |url=https://vimocafe.com/breaking-local-news/nclt-approves-vedantas-resolution-plan-electrosteel-lead-12407.html |access-date=17 October 2018 |publisher=Vimocafe |date=17 April 2018 |archive-date=30 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220330025949/https://vimocafe.com/breaking-local-news/nclt-approves-vedantas-resolution-plan-electrosteel-lead-12407.html |url-status=dead }} In the 1990s, as the Indian government began to sell off sick (non-performing) companies, Sterlite began to bid for them. They were able to bid successfully for [[Bharat Aluminium Company|BALCO]] and [[Hindustan Zinc]] Limited, both bankrupt companies that had been closed down for 4 years. Meanwhile, in January 1993, D. P. Agarwal founded Twinstar Holdings Limited in [[Mauritius]], which was mostly owned by Volcan investments. On 26 May 2002, the [[Enforcement Directorate]] filed a [[show cause notice]] with Sterlite, relating to the six-year period between 1993 and 1999 when Twinstar acquired the shares of Sterlite and various investment companies – such as Dwarka Prasad Anil Kumar Investments Private Limited, Pravin Navin Investment & Trading Private Limited and Sterlite Copper Rolling Mills Private Limited – which, in turn, had made substantial investments in Sterlite and another group company, Madras Aluminium Company Limited (MALCO) after obtaining permission from the [[Reserve Bank of India]] (RBI). On 29 April 1999, many of these investment companies were liquidated and all the shares of Sterlite came back to Twinstar's possession. Twinstar became the 100% owner of shares in these investment companies and received government approvals from the RBI as well as the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB). On 8 December 1999, officials of the Income Tax department raided the offices of Sterlite located at Dhanraj Mahal, [[Apollo Bunder]] and [[Nariman Point|Tulsiani Chambers]], [[Mumbai]], and seized many documents. The IT department then decided to engage the services of ED officials as it appeared that there could have been a violation of the country's foreign exchange laws. After analyzing these documents, the ED inferred that Twinstar was incorporated with the sole intention of acquiring an interest in Sterlite. The Directorate alleged that the Agarwals, before liquidating the shares of the investment companies mentioned, had written off loans worth 230 million and made an agreement to gift their overseas corporate body, Twinstar, a sum of {{INR}}338 million including shares of Sterlite worth {{INR}}72 million. Between 1993 and 1999, Sterlite and its investment companies allegedly brought in {{INR}}2.08 billion to India through Twinstar to subscribe to the shares of Sterlite and make investments in the company.{{cite news |title=Chidambaram faces flak on Vedanta links |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/economy-policy/chidambaram-faces-flak-on-vedanta-links-106080901010_1.html |access-date=17 October 2018 |work=Business Standard|date=26 February 2013}} ===Sesa Goa – Scambi (1954–1963)=== The company today known as Sesa Goa was founded in 1954, as '''Scambi Economici SA Goa'''.{{Cite web|url=http://profit.ndtv.com/Corporate/Company-History/100295/Sesa-Goa-Ltd-?microslug=livebudget2012|title = Business News, Market Updates, Economy, Finance, Stock, BSE, NSE, Nifty – NDTV Profit}} Since then, it gradually grew to become a large low-cost producer of iron ore. During 1991–1995, it diversified into the manufacture of [[pig iron]] and [[metallurgical]] [[coke (fuel)|coke]]. Scambi Economici Societa Anonyma (SESA), owned by Baron Ludovic Toeplitz, with the financial backing of Alessandro Vassalo, obtained the Orasso Dongor mining lease in Sirsaim, Goa in 1954 and Sesa Goa Limited was formed. It was bought over in 1955, with equal shareholding, by Gewerkeshaft Exploration e Bergbau and Ferromin S.p.A., a subsidiary of [[Ilva (company)|Finsider S.p.A.]] (of [[Istituto per la Ricostruzione Industriale|IRI group]]), which eventually acquired the other half stake in 1963.{{citation needed|date=July 2024}} ===Sesa Goa (1963–2007)=== Sesa Goa Limited was incorporated as a private limited company in 1963 under the [[Companies Act, 1956]]. In 1979, Sesa Goa Private Limited was formed, with the merger of Sesa Goa Limited with another mining company in Goa, Mingoa Sociedade Miniera Goesa S.a.r.l. By 1965, Sesa Goa and Mingoa were incorporated as a [[private limited company]] under the Companies Act, 1956. The [[Mergers and acquisitions|merger]] happened in 1979 and the new, unified company was called 'Sesa Goa Pvt Ltd'. The company went public in 1981{{cite web |url=http://www.valuenotes.com/print-article.php?aid=MTQ5NzM2 |title=Sesa Goa: Volume expansion to drive growth |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/lh5h?url=http://www.valuenotes.com/print-article.php?aid=MTQ5NzM2 |archive-date=14 September 2012 |access-date=5 June 2017}} with 42,000 Indian [[shareholder]]s, holding 60% of its [[Share (finance)|shares]] and the remaining 40% held by Finsider International, which later became [[Ilva (company)|ILVA International]]. Sesa Goa had started with iron mining as its core business but slowly, it ventured into barge construction in 1984 at Sirsaim, located in the [[Bardez]] [[taluka]] of North Goa. Since then, the barge construction unit has been developed into a shipbuilding division.{{Cite web |url=http://www.edelweiss.in/market/Information.aspx?co_code=502&tb=CH |title=Edelweiss |access-date=22 March 2012 |archive-date=8 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110808150821/http://www.edelweiss.in/market/Information.aspx?co_code=502&tb=CH |url-status=dead }} In the 1990s, Sesa Goa began further expansion, aided by an influx of foreign investment during the [[Economic liberalisation in India|economic liberalization of India]] enforced by the [[World Bank]] and [[IMF]]. In 1992, the first phase of a 150,000 [[ton]] [[pig iron]] plant was commissioned. In the same year, Sesa introduced India's first low-[[phosphorus]] [[foundry]] grade pig iron in India and subsequently formalised the business under pig iron division. The pig iron plant was located at [[Amona, Goa|Amona]], [[Goa]] and had an annual production capacity of 250,000 tonnes per annum. Other alliances were formed in the nineties—in January 1995, Sesa Shipping was launched by acquiring a transhipper ''M.V. Orissa''. The year also saw the inclusion of 84 new [[coke (fuel)|coke]] ovens. When Mitsui & Co. of Japan bought Finsider International in 1996, it gained 51% stake in Sesa Go. By 1997, Sesa Kembla became a 100% subsidiary of Sesa Goa. In 1997, A Narrain mines located in [[Chitradurga]], [[Karnataka]] were purchased. A [[Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] directive in August 2011 led to suspension of mining activities in the region. In 1999, Sesa Goa started mining operations in [[Barbil]], which has the fifth largest deposit of iron ore and [[manganese]] in the world. They started producing iron ore which was exported from the port towns of [[Haldia]] and [[Paradip]]. During this time, the company also started the Sesa Community Development Foundation that supported the NCM Sesa Technical School and a [[football academy]] called [[SESA F.A.]] In March 2024, [[Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] also rejected a plea for reopening the plant in [[Tamil Nadu]].{{cite web |last1=Pal |first1=Priyasi |title=Sterlite Standoff: Vedanta Seeks Legal Options After SC Rejects Reopening Plea |url=https://www.brutimes.com/news/business/sterlite-standoff-vedanta-seeks-legal-options-after-sc-rejects-reopening-plea |website=Bru Times News |language=en}} During the end of the 90s, the company also began to consolidate through mergers and acquisitions. Sesa Kembla completed the creation of an indigenous and environment-friendly technology that produced high-quality metallurgical coke. This technology generated power{{cite web|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.in/2004/02/04/stories/2004020401210200.htm |title=The Hindu Business Line : FFE Minerals ties up with Sesa Kembla for coke oven |publisher=Thehindubusinessline.in |date=4 February 2004 |access-date=1 December 2016}} as a by-product.{{cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/sesa-goa-ltd/chairmanspeech/companyid-13111.cms |title=Vedanta Chairman Speech | Vedanta Ltd Chairman Speech |publisher=Economictimes.indiatimes.com |date=5 December 2012 |access-date=1 December 2016}} In 2003, the Sesa Goa equity in Sesa Industries was raised to 88.25%, impacting the shareholding pattern. ===Take over by Vedanta (2007)=== In 2007, [[Vedanta Resources]] Plc, a diversified metals and mining group founded by [[Anil Agarwal (businessman)|Anil Agarwal]], acquired 51% controlling stake{{cite news|url=http://www.hindu.com/2007/04/25/stories/2007042505011800.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070427031058/http://www.hindu.com/2007/04/25/stories/2007042505011800.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 April 2007 |title=Archive News |access-date=1 December 2016|newspaper=[[The Hindu]] |date=25 April 2007 }} in Sesa Goa Ltd. from Mitsui & Co. Ltd. Vedanta Resources is listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]] and a constituent of [[FTSE 100 Index]]. The deal was worth {{INRConvert|40.7|b}}, making it the largest M&A deal in the industry so far.{{cite web|url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/vedanta-bags-mitsuis-51-in-miner-sesa-goa/29228/ |title=Vedanta bags Mitsui's 51% in miner Sesa Goa |work=Indian Express|date=25 April 2007 |access-date=1 December 2016}} In 2009, Sesa Goa acquired Goa-based [[Dempo]] Group's mining and maritime businesses for {{INRConvert|17.5|b}} in an all-cash deal.{{cite web|author=Panaji, DHNS |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/7645/sesa-goa-buys-dempo-mining.html |title=Sesa Goa buys Dempo mining firm |publisher=Deccanherald.com |access-date=1 December 2016|date=12 June 2009 }} This was the second largest{{cite web|url=http://www.weeksupdate.com/2009/06/sesa-goa-acquires-dempo-mining.html |title=Sesa Goa acquires Dempo Mining « WeeksUpdate |publisher=Weeksupdate.com |date=21 June 2014 |access-date=1 December 2016}} acquisition in India's iron-ore industry, and it gave Sesa Goa access to Dempo's 70 million tons of iron-ore mineable resources in Goa. In 2011, Sesa Goa purchased 51% stake in Western Cluster, Liberia for $90 million.{{cite web|author=PTI |url=https://www.livemint.com/2011/08/06180728/Sesa-Goa-to-buy-51-stake-in-W.html |title=Sesa Goa to buy 51% stake in Western Cluster for $90 mn |publisher=Livemint |date=6 August 2011 |access-date=1 December 2016}} The [[Liberia Gola Forest Community]] people who also suffered from the civil war believe that the coming of Western Cluster will help to alleviate their suffering and provide employment. In 2007, it became a majority-owned subsidiary{{cite web|author=Our Bureau |url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/article2931666.ece |title=Vedanta to merge Sesa Goa, Sterlite Ind in all-share deal | Business Line |publisher=Thehindubusinessline.com |date=25 February 2012 |access-date=1 December 2016}} of [[Vedanta Resources]] Plc, listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]], when Vedanta acquired 51% controlling stake from [[Mitsui & Co.]], Ltd. In June 2009, Sesa Goa Limited acquired{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/sesa-goa-buys-dempos-mining/360847/ |title=Sesa Goa buys Dempo's mining biz | Business Standard News |publisher=Business-standard.com |access-date=1 December 2016|newspaper=Business Standard India |date=12 June 2009 }} VS Dempo & Co. Private Limited (now Sesa Resources Limited) along with its fully owned subsidiary Dempo Mining Corporation (now Vedanta Limited) and 50% equity in Goa Maritime Private Limited. In 2010, Vedanta acquired the zinc assets of British miner [[Anglo American plc]]. In 2011, [[Vedanta Resources]] bought 58.5% controlling stake in [[Cairn India]], India's largest private sector oil & gas company.{{cite web|author=Utpal Bhaskar |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/DqB65NdNYvWa7oDTVcIVHJ/Vedanta8217s-Cairn-India-stake-buy-completed.html |title=Vedanta's Cairn India stake buy completed |publisher=Livemint |date=8 December 2011 |access-date=1 December 2016}} In 2015, [[Sterlite Industries]] and [[Sesa Goa]] announced their merger and finally merged into a single entity in August 2015.{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2012-02-25/vedanta-to-merge-sterlite-industries-sesa-goa-in-all-share-transaction |title=Sesa Goa, Sterlite Combine to Reduce Debt of Parent Vedanta |website=[[Bloomberg News]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160823005141/http://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2012-02-25/vedanta-to-merge-sterlite-industries-sesa-goa-in-all-share-transaction |archive-date=23 August 2016 |access-date=5 June 2017}} In 2015, [[Sesa Sterlite]] changed its name to Vedanta Limited.{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/sesa-sterlite-renamed-as-vedanta-ltd/article7130007.ece|title=Sesa Sterlite renamed as Vedanta Ltd|date=22 April 2015|newspaper=The Hindu|access-date=1 December 2016}} On 11 April 2017, Cairn India merged with Vedanta Limited to consolidate its position as one of the largest diversified natural resources companies in the world.{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/vedanta-completes-cairn-merger/articleshow/58133946.cms|title=Cairn India merges with Vedanta|date=12 April 2017|newspaper=The Economic Times|access-date=5 June 2017}} In 2018, Vedanta Limited acquired control of Electrosteels Steels Limited.{{cite news | url = https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/vedanta-enters-steel-with-acquisition-of-electrosteel-steels-to-hold-90-118060401085_1.html | title = Vedanta enters steel with acquisition of Electrosteel Steels, to hold 90% | publisher = Business Standard, 5 June 2018 | access-date = 16 July 2018| newspaper = Business Standard India | date = 5 June 2018 | last1 = Mukul | first1 = Jyoti }} Electrosteel Steels had been constructing an integrated steel plant at [[Siyaljori]] in Jharkhand. In May 2020, it is declared that company is going to delist from Indian bourses as per the comment by Mr. Anil Agarwal.{{cite news|title=Vedanta to be delisted from Indian bourses, says Anil Agarwal|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/anil-agarwal-plans-to-delist-vedanta-from-indian-bourses-at-rs-87-a-share/articleshow/75701282.cms}} In September 2022, Vedanta signed a pact with [[Foxconn]] as a technical partner to invest {{INRConvert|1.54|t}} to set up semiconductor and display production plants in Gujarat. The venture intends to start manufacturing display and chip products within two years. The investment follows the Indian government commitment to expand incentives beyond an initial $10{{nbsp}}billion plan for those investing in [[Electronics and semiconductor manufacturing industry in India|manufacturing of semiconductors]].{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/india/vedanta-foxconn-sign-mou-with-modis-home-state-20-bln-chip-foray-2022-09-13/ |title=Vedanta, Foxconn to invest $19.5 billion in India's Gujarat for chip, display project |date=13 September 2022 |work=[[Reuters]] |first1=Munsif |last1=Vengattil |first2=Aditya |last2=Kalra}}{{cite news |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-09-16/vedanta-drops-most-in-months-as-chip-factory-plan-unclear |title=Vedanta Drops Most in Months as Chip Factory Plan Unclear |date=16 September 2022 |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |first1=Divya |last1=Patil |first2=Swansy |last2=Afonso |first3=Ashutosh |last3=Joshi |url-access=limited}} Barely a year later in July 2023 the venture was ended with mutual agreement with both companies maintaining that they are still looking to set up semiconductor foundries in India.{{Cite news |date=2023-07-11 |title=Foxconn, Vedanta pull the plug on semiconductor JV |work=The Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/foxconn-vedanta-pull-the-plug-on-semiconductor-jv/articleshow/101647595.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2023-07-11 |issn=0013-0389}}{{Cite web |title=Foxconn-Vedanta: How the $19.5 billion deal went kaput |url=https://www.businessinsider.in/business/corporates/news/foxconn-vedanta-how-the-19-5-billion-deal-went-kaput/articleshow/101656453.cms |access-date=2023-07-11 |website=Business Insider}} On 24 March 2024, Vedanta Ltd announced a $6 billion investment across various business verticals, including aluminium, zinc, iron ore, steel, and oil and gas, aiming to add at least $2.5 billion to its annual [[Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization|EBITDA]]. The investment is part of a strategy involving over 50 active projects expected to generate additional revenues of over $6 billion, with plans for a significant vertical split leading to the creation of five newly listed companies.{{Cite news |date=2024-03-24 |title=Vedanta touts $6 billion investment pipeline as growth driver |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/indl-goods/svs/metals-mining/vedanta-touts-6-billion-investment-pipeline-as-growth-driver/articleshow/108744959.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-03-25 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} On 28 March 2026, Vedanta's Chairman Anil Agarwal announced the company's plans to invest nearly $5 billion in the US to "build assets, access technology and partner with the best in the industry." The company later clarified that it routinely evaluates such strategic opportunities, and any discussions regarding a potential investment are "exploratory and preliminary in nature."{{Cite web |date=2026-03-30 |title=Vedanta clarifies on report of $5 billion US investment; here's what it said - CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/vedanta-share-price-clarifies-on-report-of-usd-5-billion-us-investment-here-is-what-it-said-ws-l-19877592.htm |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=CNBCTV18 |language=en}} ==Operations== Though the company primarily operated in Goa and Karnataka, it has gradually expanded its operations in recent years to Odisha, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Jharkhand, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh.{{Cite web|url=http://www.vedantalimited.com/our-operations.aspx|title=Vedanta Limited|website=www.vedantalimited.com|access-date=5 June 2017|archive-date=10 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161110181322/http://www.vedantalimited.com/our-operations.aspx|url-status=dead}} Vedanta limited owns, leases and operates in India through the following entities: * [[Bharat Aluminium Company]]: In February 2001, Government of India in a major dis-investment deal, approved the sale of its 51% stake in BALCO to Sterlite Industries (now Vedanta Limited) for Rs.551.5 crores.{{cite web |date=17 February 2024 |title=Vedanta's Founder Anil Agarwal Net Worth |url=https://moneylaid.com/anil-agarwal-net-worth-in-rupees/ |access-date=2 April 2024 |work=[[Money Laid]]}} The government of India owns the remaining 49.0%. Incorporated in 1965, BALCO was a profit making Public Sector Company which had played a crucial role in increasing the usage of aluminium over a wide spectrum of products ranging from household utensils to aerospace and defense sectors. BALCO is headquartered at [[Korba, Chhattisgarh|Korba]] in the state of [[Chhattisgarh]] and is a vertically integrated aluminium producer having its own captive bauxite mines, captive power plants and smelter.{{cite web|url=http://www.frontline.in/static/html/fl1806/18060240.htm|title=Battle over Balco|publisher=Frontline|access-date=28 April 2017}} * [[Hindustan Zinc]]: HZL is headquartered in [[Udaipur]] in the state of [[Rajasthan]]. HZL's equity shares are listed and traded on the NSE and BSE. Vedanta owns 64.9% of the share capital in HZL and has management control. Sterlite has a call option to acquire the government of India's remaining ownership interest.{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Money/doyLFuwB5gJVUzNY0UGt9K/Getting-hold-of-Hindustan-Zincs-cash-turning-an-expensive-a.html|title=Getting hold of Hindustan Zinc's cash turning an expensive affair for Vedanta|date=24 March 2017|publisher=Live mint|access-date=28 April 2017}} * [[Sterlite Copper]] ([[Tuticorin]]):{{cite web |title=Our operations |url=http://vedantalimited.com/our-operations.aspx |website=www.vedantalimited.com |publisher=Vedanta limited |access-date=30 September 2018 |archive-date=30 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930154516/http://vedantalimited.com/our-operations.aspx |url-status=dead }} Sterlite is registered office headquartered in [[Tuticorin]], [[Tamil Nadu]], India. Sterlite has been a public listed company in India since 1988, and its equity shares are listed and traded on the NSE and the BSE, and are also listed and traded on the NYSE in the form of ADSs. Vedanta owns 53.9% of Sterlite and has management control of the company. Protest by Public of Tuticorin started for not following Environmental Clearance Issues. The Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB) accused the factory of releasing noxious gas in the air. It said sulphur-di-oxide levels had gone off the charts on the night of 23 March in the year 2013. It showed a reading of 2939.55 mg/cubic metre against the prescribed limit of 1250 mg/ cubic metre more people were affected by cancer and other breathing disorders but the Indian government did not take any action.{{cite news |url=https://www.deccanherald.com/content/322671/vedantas-copper-smelting-plant-ordered.html |title=Vedanta's copper smelting plant ordered to stop operations Vedanta star, a holding company){{cite news | url = https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/vedanta-enters-steel-with-acquisition-of-electrosteel-steels-to-hold-90-118060401085_1.html | title = Vedanta enters steel with acquisition of Electrosteel Steels, to hold 90% | newspaper = Business Standard India | date = 5 June 2018 | publisher = Business Standard, 5 June 2018 | access-date = 16 October 2018| last1 = Mukul | first1 = Jyoti }} * [[Talwandi Sabo Power Project|Talwandi Sabo power limited]] (a [[thermal power plant]] in Mansa, near [[Bathinda]], [[Punjab]]){{cite web |title=Invitation for EOI |url=https://tsplindia.co/RFP-Cement-allied-product-unit.pdf |website=Talwandi Sabo Power Limited website |publisher=Vedanta Limited |access-date=17 October 2018 |archive-date=17 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017123711/https://tsplindia.co/RFP-Cement-allied-product-unit.pdf |url-status=dead }} * [[Vedanta Aluminium]]: Vedanta Aluminium is headquartered in [[Jharsuguda]], [[Odisha]]. Vedanta owns 70.5% of the share capital of Vedanta Aluminium and Sterlite owns the remaining 29.5% share capital of Vedanta Aluminium. Vedanta Aluminium produces ingots, billets & wire rods that are sold in the markets around the world. Vedanta Aluminium Limited (VAL) has acquired a 24.5% stake in L & T subsidiary Raykal Aluminium. Based on achieving certain milestones, Vedanta Aluminium will fully acquire Raykal Aluminium in phases.{{cite news| url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/article3515627.ece | title=Vedanta Aluminium acquires 24.5% stake in L&T subsidiary | date=11 June 2012}} Vedanta is undertaking an expansion program. It plans to produce around 1.5 million tonnes of aluminium in the fiscal year 2016-17 from its [[Jharsuguda]] and [[Korba, Chhattisgarh|Korba]] smelters which will make it the largest aluminium producer in India. Its alumina refinery, located in Lanjigarh, plans{{Cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/vedanta-revives-second-stream-operations-at-lanjigarh-refinery-116080801047_1.html|title=Vedanta revives second stream operations at Lanjigarh refinery}} to produce 1.5 million tonnes of alumina and depending on availability of domestic bauxite will subsequently ramp it up to 4 million tonnes per annum in the near future.{{Cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/vedanta-to-produce-1-5-mn-tonnne-aluminium-in-fy17-116052001186_1.html|title=Vedanta to produce 1.5 mn tonnne aluminium in FY17|last=Dash|first=Jayajit|newspaper=Business Standard India|date=20 May 2016|publisher=Business Standard|access-date=20 May 2016}} Despite NGO sponsored activism, the Lanjigarh smelter has seen a lot of support from the local people who see it as an important source of employment and livelihood.{{Cite web|url=http://www.orissadiary.com/ShowBussinessNews.asp?id=68725|title=Pro-Development Demonstration by Dongaria Tribals|website=Orissadiary|access-date=3 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160804215020/http://www.orissadiary.com/ShowBussinessNews.asp?id=68725|archive-date=4 August 2016|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}} **Madras Aluminium Company: MALCO is headquartered in Mettur, India. MALCO's equity shares are listed and traded on the NSE and BSE. It owns 93.9% of MALCO's share capital and has management control of the company.{{cite web|url=https://www.mettur.com/companys/malco.html|title=Madras Aluminium Company Limited|publisher=Mettur|access-date=28 April 2017}} ==Shareholding pattern== As of 30 June 2018, the company is owned 50% by the promoters (under Finsider international and Twinstar holding, both holding companies owned under the names of 12 members of the Agarwal family) and 50% by the public. The promoters ownership (51%) is held under "Westglobe limited" under "Twinstar holdings" (37%) and Finsider international (11%).{{cite web |title=Vedanta limited shareholding pattern (September 2018) – Pages 4 and 5 |url=https://www.vedantalimited.com/InvestorRelationDoc/vedl_shareholding_pattern_q1_equity_shares.pdf |website=Vedanta official website |publisher=Vedanta Limited |access-date=17 October 2018 |archive-date=17 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017082303/https://www.vedantalimited.com/InvestorRelationDoc/vedl_shareholding_pattern_q1_equity_shares.pdf |url-status=dead }} The balance 49% of the company is owned by mutual funds ([[ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund|ICICI Prudential]]), foreign portfolio investors (17%), Corporate bodies (7%), [[LIC India]] (6%), Citibank New York (4%), individual retail shareholders (5%) and Citibank NYADR (4%).{{cite web |title=Share holding pattern – Vedanta Limited, India |url=http://www.vedantalimited.com/media/128025/vedl_shareholding_pattern_q1_equity_shares.pdf |website=www.vedantalimited.com |publisher=Vedanta official / letter to SEBI |access-date=30 September 2018 |archive-date=30 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180930154658/http://www.vedantalimited.com/media/128025/vedl_shareholding_pattern_q1_equity_shares.pdf |url-status=dead }} Relationship with [[Sesa Goa]]: Sesa Goa was originally a [[Portuguese people|Portuguese]] owned company, with iron ore mines in Goa. In the 1990s, Sesa Goa was purchased by Sterlite industries (subsequently renamed as Vedanta Limited).{{cite news |title=Sterlite – Sesa Goa merger |url=http://smartinvestor.business-standard.com/BSCMS/PDF/sesagoa_290212.pdf |access-date=17 October 2018 |agency=Smart Investor |publisher=IIFL / Business Standard |date=28 February 2012}} Vedanta Management has shared its intentions to delist company from stock exchanges subject to Shareholders approval. However, delisting is a lengthy process and may take years.{{Cite web|title=Vedanta board approves proposed de-listing from BSE, NSE|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/vedanta-board-approves-proposed-de-listing-from-bse-nse-5284511.html|website=Moneycontrol|date=18 May 2020 |access-date=2020-05-19}} Relationship with Cairns India and Carins energy: In 2016, Cairns India and Cairns Energy were purchased by Vedanta Limited. Cairns was a US-owned company and the 2nd largest private oil and gas company in India. ==Products == '''Copper''': Vedanta limited operates the largest [[Smelter|copper smelter]] In India, in [[Tuticorin]]. This contributes to nearly 50% of Vedanta Limited's profits. In early 2016, due to local protests related to environment pollution, the plant was temporarily shut down by the Tamil Nadu state government. Vedanta has contested these claims, stating that its gas emissions are well below the state norms and the emissions of 11 other neighboring industries. It has also stated that their plant does not pump any water into the sea, due to a change in the plant configuration after a previous (2013) complaints from the state government.{{cite web |title=FAQ on Sterlite Copper – updated 17th September 2018 |url=https://www.vedantalimited.com/MediaDocuments/FAQs_on_Sterlite_Copper_Updated_17thSept2018.pdf |website=www.vedantalimited.com |publisher=Vedanta Limited (Press release) |access-date=17 October 2018 |archive-date=17 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181017082359/https://www.vedantalimited.com/MediaDocuments/FAQs_on_Sterlite_Copper_Updated_17thSept2018.pdf |url-status=dead }} '''Zinc-Lead-Silver''': Zinc India business is owned and operated by [[Hindustan Zinc Limited]] (HZL). HZL owns and operates a fully integrated zinc-lead business. HZL is one of the world's largest integrated zinc-lead producers by volume. Sesa Sterlite owns 64.9% of the share capital of HZL, while the Government of India remains an equity partner and holds a 29.5% stake. HZL is listed on Indian stock exchanges (NSE and BSE).HZL's fully integrated zinc operations include five lead-zinc mines, one rock phosphate mine, four hydrometallurgical zinc smelters, two lead smelters, one lead-zinc smelter, four sulphuric acid plants, one silver refinery and six captive power plants at our Chanderiya, Dariba and Zawar facilities in the State of Rajasthan, processing and refining facilities for zinc at Haridwar and for zinc, lead and silver at Pantnagar, both in the State of Uttarakhand and in northern India. In FY 2013, these operations delivered 870,000 tonnes of mined zinc-lead metal-in-concentrate, and 802,000 tonnes of refined zinc and lead.{{cite news |title=Zinc day – production to grow after hiatus of 6 years |url=http://static-news.moneycontrol.com/static-mcnews/2017/09/04-09-2017-50.pdf |access-date=17 October 2018 |agency=Motilal Oswal |publisher=Money Control |date=1 September 2017 |archive-date=18 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918171619/http://static-news.moneycontrol.com/static-mcnews/2017/09/04-09-2017-50.pdf |url-status=dead }} '''Aluminium''': Vedanta's aluminium output rises 2% to 584,000 tonnes in second Qtr of FY23{{cite news |title=Vedanta's aluminium output rises |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/vedanta-s-aluminium-output-rises-2-to-584-000-tonnes-in-second-qtr-of-fy23-122100301194_1.html}} == Controversies== ===2001 SEBI case=== In 2001, Sterlite industries, [[BPL Group|BPL]] and [[Videocon]] were found guilty by the Securities Exchange Board of India ([[SEBI]]) of having colluded with the broker [[Harshad Mehta]] and 17 brokers (10 from [[Bombay Stock Exchange|BSE]] and 7 from [[National Stock Exchange of India|NSE]]) in a bid to corner shares and rig shares prices. This resulted in a ban on Sterlite from accessing capital markets for 2 years.{{cite web |title=Press release – Ref.No.PR 71/2001 (19 April 2001) |url=https://www.sebi.gov.in/media/press-releases/apr-2001/action-against-harshad-mehta-videocon-bpl-and-sterlite_17608.html |website=www.sebi.gov.in |publisher=SEBI |access-date=17 October 2018}} Subsequent to this, in 2003, [[Vedanta Resources]] (UK) was listed on the [[London Stock Exchange]]. Vedanta Resources itself is a holding company that owns many entities including a large proportion of Vedanta Limited and Sterlite industries.{{cite web |title=16 years of fraud? |url=https://www.minesandcommunities.org/article.php?a=9685 |website=www.minesandcommunities.org |publisher=Mines and communities |access-date=17 October 2018}} ===Tuticorin Sterlite protests=== In early 2018, thousands of residents of [[Tuticorin]] began to protest against the Sterlite plant located in the industrial complex there. The protests continued for three months and began to draw the attention of the media as well as local political parties who began to instigate as well as mobilise locals. Most of the protests were related to what locals perceived to be pollution from the Sterlite factory. The managers of Sterlite countered that there were another four similar plants adjacent to them, and that they were complying with all government regulations. There was little equipment, either with the plant or with the government to take actual measurements of the air in the vicinity. Sterlite further countered that contrary to the rumours that were being circulated, they did not pump any water from the plant into the sea which lay more than 10 kilometers away. In April 2018, the Government of Tamil Nadu placed an order to close down the factory.{{cite web |title=Sterlite copper – Know the truth |url=https://www.sterlitecopper.com/know-the-truth/ |website=www.sterlitecopper.com |publisher=Sterlite Copper |access-date=17 October 2018}} This order was temporarily cancelled by the district collector.{{cite web | url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/tuticorin-anti-sterlite-protest-power-cut-for-vedanta-owned-sterlite-in-tuticorin-10-latest-facts-1857089 | title=Power Cut for Vedanta-Owned Sterlite in Tuticorin: 10 Latest Facts }}{{cite news | url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/sterlite-s-pollution-problem-113041801267_1.html | title=Sterlite's pollution problem | newspaper=Business Standard India | date=18 April 2013 | last1=Narasimhan | first1=T. E. }} In May 2018, amidst ongoing protests by thousands of people, matters turned rough one day and the police opened fire on demonstrators.{{cite web | url=https://www.dinamalar.com/news/tamil-nadu-district-news-thoothukudi/news/2027846 | title=தூத்துக்குடியில் இயல்பு நிலை திரும்பியது | date=25 May 2018 }}{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-44234715 | title=India shuts Tamil Nadu smelting plant after deadly protests | work=BBC News | date=24 May 2018 }} The firing killed 13 people and protesters turned violent, burning vehicles and structures. Residents say the copper smelter is causing environmental damage. Subsequent to the firing, the Tamil Nadu chief minister [[Edappadi K. Palaniswami|Palaniswami]] ordered a judicial inquiry into the shootings but defended the police response.{{cite web | url=https://www.firstpost.com/india/sterlite-protest-live-updates-palaniswami-govt-appeals-against-madras-hc-order-to-preserve-bodies-of-thoothukudi-victims-4480617.html | title=Sterlite protest updates: 13 people killed, 102 others wounded, confirms new Thoothukudi district collector | date=24 May 2018 }} == 2023-26 Demerger == In September 2023, Vedanta Limited announced a demerger plan to separate its businesses into independent listed entities. Following revisions to the proposal, the company outlined a structure under which Vedanta Limited would be divided into four sector-focused companies, comprising [[aluminium]], [[oil and gas]], [[power]], and [[iron and steel]] businesses, while certain other operations would remain within the parent entity. Under the scheme, shareholders of Vedanta Limited would receive shares in each of the resulting companies in proportion to their existing holdings. The company stated that the restructuring was intended to simplify its corporate structure, enhance management focus, improve capital allocation, and enable each business to pursue its own growth strategy. The demerger was fulky approved in early 2026, by regulatory authorities. In June 2026, the demerged companies were listed on [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] and [[National Stock Exchange]]{{Cite news |date=2026-06-15 |title=Vedanta Demerger Highlights: 4 new entities get listed; Vedanta Aluminium, Oil & Gas, Iron & Steel shares slip 5% each|url=https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/vedanta-demerger-live-vedanta-aluminium-vedanta-power-vedanta-oil-gas-vedanta-iron-steel-shares-listing-15-j-11781492509883.html |access-date=2026-06-15 |work=livemint |language=en}} === Demerger Plan Objections === In August 2025, Vedanta's proposed demerger plan faced significant objections from the Indian federal government and the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The government raised concerns over concealed liabilities and incomplete disclosures, leading the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) to defer the hearing to September 17, 2025.{{Cite news |date=2025-08-20 |title=Indian miner Vedanta's demerger faces government objection, CNBC-TV18 reports |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/india/indian-miner-vedantas-demerger-faces-government-objection-cnbc-tv18-reports-2025-08-20/ |access-date=2025-08-20 |work=Reuters |language=en}} SEBI issued a warning regarding modifications made to the demerger scheme post-No Objection Certificate (NOC).{{Cite news |last=Kumar |first=Shivendra |date=2025-08-20 |title=Vedanta shares slip 3% after reports of govt objection to demerger, Sebi's warning |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/vedanta-shares-slip-3-after-reports-of-govts-objection-to-demerger-plan-sebis-warning/articleshow/123405924.cms |access-date=2025-08-20 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} ==See also== * [[Mining in India]] * [[List of mines in India]] {{Portal bar|Companies|India}} ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== * {{official website|http://www.vedantalimited.com/}} * [https://www.vedantaresources.com// Group homepage] {{Use dmy dates|date=September 2019}} {{Vedanta Resources}} {{Energy companies and organisations in India}} {{DJSI World}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Iron ore mining in India]] [[Category:Vedanta Resources]] [[Category:Companies based in Goa]] [[Category:1950s establishments in Portuguese India]] [[Category:Indian companies established in 1954]] [[Category:1954 establishments in the Portuguese Empire]] [[Category:Iron ore mining companies of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange]] [[Category:Mining companies of India]] [[Category:Oil and gas companies of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the National Stock Exchange of India]] [[Category:Companies listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange]]
